**TL;DR** — The PR is a well-engineered, safe-to-merge foundation. Data modelling, matching semantics, pruning, migration, and fail-closed error handling are all correct. One P3 contract-drift finding: `transport` and `auth_mode` are documented v2 schema fields and verified in unit isolation, but the sole production call site in `github.py:post_review_to_github` never passes them to `build_sticky_comment`, so every real v2 blob will carry empty strings for both fields indefinitely.

### Findings (1)

🟡 **P3** · `contract-drift` — **`transport`/`auth_mode` never wired at production call site** · `lintro/ai/review/github.py:102`

<details><summary>Details</summary>

🟡 **P3** · `contract-drift` · `high confidence`

### `transport`/`auth_mode` never wired at production call site

The v2 RunRecord schema documents `transport` and `auth_mode` as per-run statistics. `build_sticky_comment` was extended to accept both parameters and `test_sticky_records_transport_and_auth_mode` validates them by calling `build_sticky_comment` directly. However, the sole production call site — `post_review_to_github` — passes `prior_state` and `head_sha=result.metadata.head_ref` but omits `transport` and `auth_mode`, so both fields are `""` in every real v2 blob. Any downstream surface (#1907–#1912) that renders transport or auth mode will always show empty values.

<details><summary>💡 Why this matters & how to fix</summary>

**Cause:** `build_sticky_comment` added `transport: str = ""` and `auth_mode: str = ""` as optional parameters. The production caller was updated for the other new parameters but not these two. The unit test exercises them in isolation, masking the wiring gap.

**Fix:** Pass `transport` and `auth_mode` in `post_review_to_github` from the review execution context (add fields to `ReviewMetadata`, or thread them from the transport selection layer). Alternatively, add a test that calls the full `post_review_to_github` path and asserts the persisted `RunRecord` carries the expected transport value, making the gap immediately visible.

</details>
